speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the past few decades, we are observing upward trends in rainfall intensities and frequency of heavy rain events.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This, coupled with growing urbanisation which increases stormwater run-off, has made flood management more challenging.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To reduce flood risk, the Public Utilities Board (PUB) adopts a holistic "source-pathway-receptor" approach that addresses flood protection, not just through drains and canals, that is, the pathway; but also in areas generating stormwater run-off, that is, the source; and areas where floods may occur, that is, the receptor.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has also been carrying out improvement works to progressively increase the capacity of existing drains and canals and rehabilitate older drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the last three years, drainage improvement works at 192 locations have been completed and there are ongoing projects at 90 other locations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Given land scarcity, we cannot rely solely on more and bigger drains to mitigate floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As such, PUB also requires developers to implement "source" solutions to better manage storm-water discharges from developments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These include on-site detention measures for larger developments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, PUB also requires "receptor" solutions, such as higher platform levels, crest protection and flood barriers, especially for critical installations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These help to protect developments when floods occur.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Keeping our drains free flowing is the joint responsibility of all stakeholders, be they public agencies, private developers and contractors, and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB works closely with the National Environment Agency’s (NEA) Department of Public Cleanliness to regularly remove debris, litter and leaves from the drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It also encourages the public to keep our environment litter-free and give feedback on drain conditions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In reply to Mr Ang Wei Neng's question, PUB does indeed work with the major development agencies to get their contractors to conduct checks on the public drains near their construction sites to ensure that the drains are free of debris.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is supplemented by PUB's audit checks on approved drainage works on site.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During critical stages, such as drainage diversion works and decommissioning of existing drains, more frequent checks are carried out.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB also leverages on technology, for example, closed circuit television (CCTV) cameras, to facilitate the monitoring of work sites.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Ang mentioned the recent flash floods, of which one recent occurrence is at Upper Thomson Road.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has investigated and found out that it was due to unauthorised work, which affected our public drainage system.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB takes a serious view of such unauthorised works and will not hesitate to take action against errant parties under the Sewerage and Drainage Act.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Such penalties and reputational damage, as well as being liable for civil penalties if they cause third-party damage, have been sufficient and effective in the past, and PUB will continue to review the amounts from time to time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While PUB continues with efforts to reduce flood risks, we should be realistic to note that it is not possible to eliminate floods altogether.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Localised conditions, exceptionally heavy downpour, tides and errant behaviour all contribute to flash floods now and then.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As such, our focus is also to help members of the public better manage floods when they occur.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To this end, PUB has put in place monitoring and alert systems to keep the public updated, through a network of water level sensors and CCTVs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Members of the public can subscribe to receive SMS alerts from selected water level sensors via PUB's website.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These sensors are placed in flood-prone areas and hotspots, and could provide the public with early information on the rising water levels in drains in selected flood-prone areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the event of a flash flood, PUB works closely with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the Police to monitor road conditions and provide real-time updates on PUB's Facebook and Twitter pages and via radio broadcast, as well as LTA's Expressway Monitoring Advisory System (EMAS) on the roads.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our stormwater management strategies have served us well.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB will continue its efforts to reduce flood-prone areas and ensure the proper functioning of the drainage system.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, measures, such as drain upgrading, canals and centralised detention tanks, take time to implement and may not be able to cope with all extremities in rainfall.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As such, I urge all parties to play a part in ensuring that our drains are free-flowing, and to appreciate the importance of source and receptor requirements in their developments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Through concerted efforts, we can minimise flood risks and better manage flood events.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The Minister mentioned about improvements to pathways in 90 locations.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Recently, there were floods in Paya Lebar and Tanjong Pagar, besides Upper Thomson.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, are Paya Lebar and Tanjong Pagar part of the 90 locations?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The second clarification is: the Minister mentioned that for the flood at Upper Thomson, PUB had concluded that the errant contractor diverted the drainage and caused the flood.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, has PUB taken action to prosecute the contractor?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Drainage improvement works have been ongoing in Geylang River.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The flood protection to Paya Lebar areas will be enhanced then.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the action against the contractor, we are taking steps right now to put up the charges.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will be investigating and putting up the charges when we are ready.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: What is the danger that some of these unauthorised works and the impact that they have on the drainage system will not be discovered until way into the future?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The temporary diversion constructed by the contractor within the worksite was under-sized.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: More importantly, it did not inform PUB before commencement of works.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The public drainage system across Upper Thomson Road was also found to be altered by the contractor without PUB's approval.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB, therefore, will be taking action against the contractor.
